3.  Resolution Approving and Adopting an Amended Conflict of Interest Code Pursuant to
  the Political Reform Act of 1974
  Pursuant to the Political Reform Act, the City is to: 1) Conduct a review of the City’s
  Conflict of Interest Code to determine if a change in the Code was necessary: 2) file a
  biennial notice regarding the results of the review no later than the required deadline; and
  3) amend the City’s Code pursuant to the Act, if necessary.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution approving and adopting the amended Conflict of Interest Code
  pursuant to the Political Reform Act of 1974.

4.  Long Beach Unified School District (LBUSD) Master Facility Use Agreement
  Due to the lack of recreational resources, the City and LBUSD have developed a Master
  Facility Use Agreement to combine facility resources to benefit our community. This
  agreement allows the City to utilize Avalon Schools’ gymnasium, baseball field,
  auditorium, and class spaces in exchange for the utilization of City facilities such as Joe
  Machado Field, public parks, Tremont Hall, and available meeting spaces at City Hall.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute a Master Facility Use Agreement with LBUSD and
  Avalon Schools.

5.  Appeal of the Decision of the Vehicle Hearing Officer: Denial of a Request for an
  Oversized Commercial Autoette
  John Jackson, on behalf of Eagle Electric, submitted an application for a commercial
  autoette permit. The application also indicated Eagle Electric/Jackson was seeking an
  oversized vehicle. The application was considered by the Vehicle Hearing Officer on
  August 19, 2022. As there is no designation for an “oversized” commercial autoette within
  the Avalon Municipal Code! the Vehicle Hearing Officer formally denied the request on
  August 24, 2022.
  Recommended Action
  1. Open the Public Hearing. 2. Receive Public Comment, 3. Close the Public Hearing. 4.
  Consider applicant’s appeal and determine to either a.) Uphold the decision of the Vehicle
  Hearing Officer; b.) Overturn the decision of the Vehicle Hearing Officer; or c.) Modify the
  decision of the Vehicle Hearing Officer.

SUBJECT:  Resolution Approving and Adopting an Amended Conflict of Interest
  Code Pursuant to the Political Reform Act of 1974

RECOMMENDATION: Adopt a resolution approving and adopting the amended Conflict of
Interest Code pursuant to the Political Reform Act of 1974.

REPORT SUMMARY: The Political Reform Act of 1974, Government Code Section 81000 et
seq. (the Act). requires all public agencies to adopt and maintain a Conflict of Interest Code.
The Act further requires that agencies regularly review and update their Codes as necessary
when directed by the code-reviewing body or when change is necessitated by changed
circumstances (Sections 87306 and 87306.5). As the City’s code-reviewing body, the City
Council directed that the Code be reviewed as required under the Act. During this review, staff

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to execute a Master Facility Use
Agreement with LBUSD and Avalon Schools.

REPORT SUMMARY: Due to the lack of recreational resources, the City of Avalon and Long
Beach Unified School District (LBUSD) have developed a Master Facility Use Agreement to
combine resources to benefit our community. This allows the City to utilize Avalon Schools’
gymnasium, baseball field, auditorium, and class spaces in exchange for the utilization of City
facilities such as Joe Machado Field, public parks, Tremont Hall, and available meeting spaces
at City Hall.

The last Agreement expired in 2018 and needed to be updated. Both parties have been
working in good faith to negotiate a new agreement while allowing for use of spaces during the
contract development process.

The proposed agreement will be a flexible contract to be used in perpetuity, with clauses to
allow amendments based on working conditions.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Enhance Recreational Opportunities.

FISCAL IMPACTS: N/A

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City would not be
able to utilize LBUSD properties for community programming.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Submit agreement to LBUSD Board of Directors finalize.

REPORT SUMMARY: On May 19, 2021, John Jackson, on behalf of Eagle Electric, submitted
an application for a new commercial autoette permit. The application also indicated Eagle
Electric/Jackson was seeking an oversized vehicle. The application was considered by the
Vehicle Hearing Officer on August 19, 2022.

As there is no designation for an oversized” commercial autoette within the Avalon Municipal
Code (AMC), the Vehicle Hearing Officer formally denied the request on August 24, 2022. See
findings of fact and conclusions of Law attached hereto.

PerAMC Section 1-4.01 (b), Except as otherwise specifically provided in this Code, any person
excepting to any decision made by any official of the City Pursuant to any of the provisions of
this Code may appeal in writing to the Council by filing with the City Clerk a written notice of such
appeal setting forth the specific grounds thereof.”

The provisions for granting a commercial autoette permit are defined within AMC Section 4-
4.1703 (c) as follows:

Commercial Autoette Permits. One commercial autoette permit may be granted to any person,
organization, partnership, trust or corporation for use in connection with a commercial enterprise
located within the City limits or within three miles of the City limits, without being subject to a
waiting period, as follows:
   IlL The following findings must be made in an affirmative manner
  a. The commercial autoette for which a permit is requested is necessary to the
  proper functioning of the commercial enterprise.
  b. The commercial enterprise has no other vehicle, autoette or other source of
  transportation that can reasonably satisfy its transportation requirements, including
  resident vehicles and autoettes.
  c.That the autoette measures no more than 130 inches in length, including the
  front and rear bumpers.
  d.The commercial enterprise is a significant source of income to the applicant and
  not a side business or hobby, or the Hearing Officer determines that shared use of
  the autoette by two or more businesses owned by the permittee is consistent with
  the purposes and goals of this chapter, or the autoette is to be used on a full-time
  basis or an exclusive basis for a business venture or ventures by the permittee.

The Vehicle Hearing Officer made the finding that Eagle Electric/Jackson is eligible for a
commercial autoette permit. However, the proposed autoette exceeds the maximum length of
an autoette. While the AMC allows for oversized vehicles (Section 4-4.1705.1), it does not allow
for oversized autoettes. In case an autoette does not fulfill the needs of a business, the AMC
allows for a commercial business to apply for a commercial vehicle permit. However, the current
wait list for a commercial vehicle is significant.

In 2021, the City Council discussed autoette size during four regular City Council Meetings.
Discussions resulted in redefining the length of an autoette from 120” to 130”. Additionally, per
City Council direction, autoettes currently registered in the City of Avalon that exceeded the
newly established 130” were granted “grandfathered” status on the condition that they would not
be sold or registered to any other owner in Avalon. At the time the ordinance was adopted, 18

The autoette proposed by Eagle Electric, a Polaris Gem, is 55.5” wide by 146” long.

and does not comply with the autoette or Low-Speed Vehicle/Neighborhood Electric Vehicle as
defined in either California Vehicle Code 385.5 or 49 CRE 571.500 as existed on January 1,
2010.

City Staff supports the findings of the Vehicle Hearing Officer in as much as the decision is
consistent with the AMC.

§ 4-4.1701. Findings.
The Council hereby determines that there are special problems existing in the City relatng to the size
and nature of the streets and the characteristics and nature of the City itself and, in view of these
special problems, the Council hereby determines that special rules regulating the size, number, noise,
speed, and classes of vehicles used, permitted, or operated on the streets under its jurisdiction are
necessary. In furtherance thereof, and in order to provide and maintain accurate and complete records
and information upon which appropriate rules and regulations may be determined, the provisions of this
article are enacted.

REPORT SUMMARY: This item was originally heard during the September 20, 2022 City
Council Meeting. City Council requested the item be continued to a future meeting.

On August 16, 2022 Daniel Mello, dba Catalina Island Golf Cart Tours, submitted a
Transportation Permit application to the City of Avalon to perform guided autoette tours.

The proposed route includes areas from the downtown area to Three Palms, Chimes Tower
Road, and Botanical Gardens.

It is stated in the application that the business will operate year-round) during daylight hours or
from 7:00 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily. The business will not have a brick-and-mortar location and be
web based. Customer’s utilizing the service will be picked-up and dropped off at prearranged
locations such as hotels, vacation rentals, etc. The operation plan includes use of two golf
  —

carts both requiring new commercial permits. If the transportation permit is approved, then
  —

will need to seek approval from the vehicle hearing officer. Upon approval, the commercially
permitted vehicle will be required to have off-street overnight parking.

Avalon Municipal Code Section (AMC) 5-14.04 requires a hearing before the City Council to
determine whether a transportation permit should be approved. Per the AMC

Sec. 5-14.04 (b)  Permits: Applications: Requirements.*

  (b)  The Council may grant a permit upon the proposed terms or upon terms other
  than those proposed. The Council shall make the initial permit grant, and the Vehicle
  Clerk may thereafter renew a permit if lie is able to make affirmative findings based on
  the criteria set forth below. If the Vehicle Clerk is unable to make the affirmative
  findings, he shall so advise the permit holder and set a hearing date before the Vehicle
  Hearing Officer, whose decision on the renewal shall be appealable to the City Council
  in accordance with the procedures set forth in Title 1, Chapter 4.:
   (1)  The applicant has presented facts demonstrating a necessity for the
  requested vehicle(s).

  (2)  The requested vehicle(s) is appropriate for the intended use and
  necessary, for the proper functioning of the applicant’s enterprise;

  (3)  The requested vehicle(s) will not have a deleterious impact on traffic
  congestion, traffic safety, noise or air pollution;

  (4)  In view of the size and nature of the streets of the City and the character of
  the City itself, the requested vehicle(s) will not have a deleterious impact on the public
  health, safety, and welfare;

  (5)  There is no more suitable alternative vehicle than the vehicle(s) requested
  by the applicant that can satisfy its requirements.

  (6) In the case of renewal only, the requested vehicle has been used and
  continues to be used in accordance with the terms and conditions of the permit.

At this time, three similar golf cart tour business are in possession of transportation permits  —

Avalon Local Tour, You be Driven, Catalina Guided Golf Cart Tours. To date, these three
operations have had negligible impacts to traffic and/or congestion. No accidents or incidents
resulting from the business have been reported to the City.

If approved by the City Council, the applicant must additionally meet the following conditions
before a permit may be issued:
  • Receive approval from the Vehicle Hearing Officer;
  • Receive approval of a business license;
  • Provide written permission from the Catalina Island Company to operate on private
  roads,
  • Agree to limit pick up and drop off locations to hotels, rental units, or requested
  locations not to include the Cabrillo Mole. and
  • Provide proof of insurance per the Avalon Municipal Code.

Upon renewal each year the Vehicle Clerk will evaluate if the business model has adversely
added to the traffic, safety, and congestion in Avalon.
